items.title: Solon Township residents push to tighten rules on proposed 800-acre data center
items.dek: Activists urge Solon Township to close loopholes allowing alternative water sources for an 800-acre hyperscale project, citing noise and health risks, as Consumers Energy says a 1GW data center is advancing through zoning.
items.findings: Proposed 800+ acre hyperscale AI data center site, per Stop Solon Township Data Center site | Consumers Energy stated in July 28, 2026 earnings meeting that a 1GW data center developer remains in local zoning processes, per activist posts | Planning Commission meeting scheduled for Wednesday, August 26, with no agenda released publicly as of the posts | No named applicant or formal project application in public records | 82% of local poll respondents said they would support recall of officials over data center handling, per Stop Solon Township Data Center survey
items.perspective: The commission has repeatedly delayed action on data center zoning while activists organize public comment. Wednesday's meeting allows public comment on ordinance changes; further readings or votes could follow at the township board level. The outcome would shape land-use rules for large power users in an area already seeing similar proposals across West Michigan townships.
items.judge_note: Document-based agenda preview of resident pressure on a specific 800-acre project with utility confirmation of scale, incremental but real.
